summary: A 1954 L-4 lookout, built from a kit to replace a 1920 cupola cabin, on Oregon's Pearsoll Peak; volunteer-restored, it survived the 2002 Biscuit Fire and opens seasonally.

facts.design: L-4 ground cab with hip roof and outriggers, built from a kit in 1954 to replace a D-6 cupola cabin of 1920

access.note: Opened each spring by the Sand Mountain Society; season June 1 to September 30. Visitors have modified the building, per the society; no posted visitor rules are in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: Last 7 miles of road take about 1.5 hours in 4-low with a high-clearance vehicle; the final 1.5 miles is a moderately difficult hiking trail.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register 5,007 ft (1,526 m); Sand Mountain Society and firelookout.com 5,098 ft (1,554 m, or 5098'). The record's elevation_m matches the register. The story gives both figures.
The 1920 cupola cabin and the 1954 L-4 cab are both part of the site's history, and firelookout.com and the register agree on both dates. The standing structure is the 1954 cab.

notes_for_editor: The 1991-2012 repair chronology rests mainly on the Sand Mountain Society page, written by the group that did the work; the register corroborates the 1954 replacement and the 1994 completion, and firelookout.com corroborates the 1920 start. The record's access 'public' is not stated outright in the sources read: the society opens the lookout each spring and says visitors have made changes, but it posts no visitor rules. Confirm before treating public visiting as established. Staffing is set to unknown; no source read describes fire staffing. The record's 2008 'modified' and 2011/2012 restorations come from the society page, so they are supported by one source. Firelookout.com places the lookout '13 miles northwest of Cave Junction' and the society places it '10 miles WNW of Selma'; the story uses the society's location. The society names the agency 'Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest'; the register says 'Siskiyou National Forest' and the story does not name the forest.
